newsitem.title: UK: Gold Outlook-Fund moves key to gold price trend.
newsitem.headline: Gold Outlook-Fund moves key to gold price trend.

text.p: How much the U.S. investment funds reduce their speculative positions on the Comex gold futures market will be the key issue for bullion prices continuing their rally, analysts said.
The gold price jumped on Friday after the funds moved in late last Thursday in New York.
On Monday morning gold was fixed at $328.05 per ounce, up from Friday's $324.20.

Gold needs to break above resistance at $330.00 an ounce to extend the current run higher, but several traders remained wary over the market's potential as consumer demand shied away from the higher prices.
"We are looking at a market that is on a bounce to nowhere," one dealer commented.
Even so, the rally continued as the funds took their profits and on the Comex open interest -- the number of unmatched positions -- fell by over 3,000 lots to 219,005 lots on Friday morning.
The open interest had been at its highest for 18 months earlier in the week with the speculative funds believed to be holding a record 90,000 lots, the equivalent of 300 tonnes of gold.
The data for last Friday will be released late Monday and analyst forecast a further fall.
The release of metal borrowed to cover the outstanding positions had made the gold market more liquid and was reflected in the lower cost of borrowing metal.
The implied one month rate was 2.15 per cent on Friday, down from 2.62 on Wednesday. The three month rate was also trimmed to 2.03 percent from 2.21 percent.

Friday's fix took gold values back to over $324.00 per ounce, the level they were at immediately before the Reserve Bank of Australia announced it had sold 167 tonnes of bullion from its reserves during the preceding six months.
That was on July 3 and the subsequent price fall was driven by the investment funds massively extending short positions in anticipation of prices reaching levels under $300.00.
That sentiment had dissipated last week after physical buying provided a price base between $315.00 and $318.00. A wobble in the hitherto rampant U.S. stock exchanges last Friday also helped gold.
But dealers and market analysts said the bounce was to be expected as gold had become seriously oversold as it plunged to 12-year lows last week.
"The bulls are jumping for joy and forecasting $330.00 per ounce. That might be possible but $340 and $350 look less likely," said market analyst Ted Arnold at Merrill Lynch.
"Until it is above the 1993 low ($326.10 fix) the market will still be selling into rallies," said bullion analyst Andy Smith at Union Bank of Switzerland.
Smith noted that a significant resistance level would be the 50-day moving average just under $340.00.
Referring to the August gold contract, Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said, "To confirm a return to the uptrend look to see resistance at $330.00 then $334.00 successfully negotiated.
" Until then we remain marginally in favour of further downside tests."
--Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
